status: review-only; not wired into the build
policy: Records omitted from this file are deliberate keeps from the source-audited translation.

changes.TT4/g0/r0: Devil: Accursed goddess! You're so ugly I could vomit!
changes.TT4/g0/r2: That must have cost a fortune…
changes.TT4/g0/r3: Athena, goddess of wisdom and guardian of Athens.
changes.TT4/g0/r4: He's unconscious. Oh no… he's not breathing!
changes.TT4/g0/r8: Priest: Thank you, Doctor! How can I ever repay you…?
changes.TT4/g0/r9: Priest: They beheaded the statue! I nearly fainted… It was probably some local thugs. What sacrilege!
changes.TT4/g0/r10: Priest: The souls of the dead descend to the underworld. I very nearly joined them myself.
changes.TT4/g0/r12: Athena: Help him… Me: B-but how? Athena: Seek the aid of the gods. Enter the underworld. He is waiting at its gate, crying out for help. Me: Who is he? Athena: Help him…
changes.TT4/g0/r20: Priest: An offering? I will accept it gratefully.
changes.TT4/g0/r23: I shake it gently. It makes a beautiful sound.
changes.TT4/g0/r29: A merchant is tending a stall.
changes.TT4/g0/r30: A plaza crowns the hill. The town spreads out below, surrounded by sea.
changes.TT4/g1/r0: He's watching the man ahead of him.
changes.TT4/g1/r1: Better watch out for a face like his.
changes.TT4/g1/r4: Beard, chest… hair everywhere. This body looks pretty old. …Doctor! Doctooor!
changes.TT4/g1/r5: Dario: There you are! Me: …! Dario: You have a patient waiting. Hurry, Dr. Nicras!
changes.TT4/g1/r8: Merchant: One silver coin. I'll take it.
changes.TT4/g1/r10: Merchant: Listen… I've got something rare. Three silver coins. Deal?
changes.TT4/g1/r11: Merchant: Buy something or move along.
changes.TT4/g1/r13: Merchant: A Persian-patterned sash embroidered with gold thread. A real treasure, eh?
changes.TT4/g1/r14: Man: You! Merchant: You're still here?! Man: Where is the boy?! Tell me! Merchant: H-help me! I found him dead! A dead man has no need for clothes! Man: What?! Merchant: At the cape, behind a rock. I swear! Man: Doctor, come with me! Me: Y-yes!
changes.TT4/g1/r15: Man: I am tutor to the young master. My name is Aristotle. We came here from Macedonia so that he might observe society for himself…
changes.TT4/g1/r16: Man: His expensive clothes should make him easy to recognize. For example… a Persian sash.
changes.TT4/g1/r17: Man: What if something has happened to him?!
changes.TT4/g1/r18: Hermes: What is it?! Me: I want to enter the underworld… Hermes: Then ask the god who rules it.
changes.TT4/g1/r22: TIME: AROUND THE 4TH CENTURY BC — PLACE: ANCIENT ATHENS — NAME: NICRAS — OCCUPATION: PHYSICIAN
changes.TT4/g1/r23: Surgical tools and medicinal herbs are scattered around.
changes.TT4/g1/r24: He seems to be my assistant.
changes.TT4/g1/r27: Dario: He knocked over a pot and scalded himself.
changes.TT4/g1/r30: Dario: More people are sick or injured. I'll look after this one. Please go examine the others.
changes.TT4/g2/r0: Youth: Much better. Here… your payment.
changes.TT4/g2/r3: Should I raise the burned area?
changes.TT4/g2/r5: How should I treat the burn?
changes.TT4/g2/r6: What should I do about the blister?
changes.TT4/g2/r13: Dario: Take the herbs. Me: Oh, right… Dario: Bill the patient once he's recovered.
changes.TT4/g2/r14: Man: May I ask… have you seen a refined-looking boy, around ten years old? Me: I'm not sure… Man: He is a young lord. I looked away for only a moment… This is terrible!
changes.TT4/g2/r15: A narrow, winding road lined with shabby houses.
changes.TT4/g2/r17: Orion: Ask him first, or he'll sulk.
changes.TT4/g2/r18: Girl: Doctor! Please… save my mother! Mother: Cough! Cough…
changes.TT4/g2/r22: Girl: I press olive oil and sell it for a living. But I have to care for Mother, so I can't even go harvest the olives.
changes.TT4/g2/r23: Girl: Her cough is gone. But… we don't have any money. I can't pay your fee. I'm sorry…
changes.TT4/g2/r24: Girl: Her cough is gone. But we have no money. I can't pay you. I pressed this olive oil myself. Please take it. Received olive oil.
changes.TT4/g2/r30: Man: Doctor… my stomach suddenly started hurting… Ugh!
changes.TT4/g2/r31: He's pale and sweating. Probably food poisoning.
changes.TT4/g3/r2: Man: Finally… the pain is easing. Thank you, Doctor.
changes.TT4/g3/r3: Man: To hell with democracy. I put my faith in the gods.
changes.TT4/g3/r9: Artemis: Whaaat? Me: I want to enter the underworld… Artemis: Beats me.
changes.TT4/g3/r17: Soldier: I am a proud warrior of Sparta! Not some soft Athenian coward!
changes.TT4/g3/r18: Soldier: Well… I injured my leg in battle. Ow! The wound is oozing pus.
changes.TT4/g3/r19: Soldier: The pain's better now. Take this in thanks. I won it in battle. He shows me a small bell. Soldier: A pharaoh once used it to ward off evil. The Warding Bell.
changes.TT4/g3/r21: The age of Greece is ending… Macedonia will soon rise to supremacy.
changes.TT4/g3/r23: Hades: Correct. I guard the underworld. Very well—you may enter.
changes.TT4/g3/r30: I stuff as many olives as I can into the bag.
changes.TT4/g4/r4: Cerberus: Yo. Me: Hello… Cerberus: This is the underworld, gateway to the dead. Me: Um… Cerberus: I know why you're here. If you want to save the child, answer my riddles. Win, and I'll set him free.
changes.TT4/g4/r5: Cerberus: Question five sages, then tell me all their names.
changes.TT4/g4/r6: Cerberus: Good. Now tell each sage his own name.
changes.TT4/g4/r8: Pythagoras is doing mathematics. He isn't beside a philosopher.
changes.TT4/g4/r9: The next man is neither Herodotus nor Plato. Ask the historian.
changes.TT4/g4/r10: The cross-legged poet is not beside Plato.
changes.TT4/g4/r11: Either Homer or Herodotus is a historian. The man at the end has a four-letter name.
changes.TT4/g4/r12: Socrates once said: No philosopher faces forward.
changes.TT4/g4/r13: Cerberus: Lucky guess. Fine. The child is free. Head back up.
changes.TT4/g4/r14: Okay… we did it… Wait. I've got a bad feeling about this!
changes.TT4/g4/r15: Devil: You little shit… Your stubborn resistance has dragged me this far. I'll give you one last chance. Accept my soul pact! Then the world will be ours. Come to me!
changes.TT4/g4/r19: Devil: Don't interfere! You followed me all the way here?! Me: Not by choice… G-give me my body back!
changes.TT4/g4/r20: Devil: Stay back! I can't move! This body belongs to me now. Give up. Me: But… Devil: Come here, boy! I'll kill you as many times as it takes!
changes.TT4/g4/r23: Devil: What?! The Warding Bell! Its peal rings through the air! Devil: Gaaaaah…!!
changes.TT4/g4/r27: Man: My lord! Can you hear the bell? Answer me! Nicras: Prince…! Man: This is Alexander, prince of Macedonia!
changes.TT4/g4/r28: Man: He's alive! Hooray!! Nicras: A miracle of the gods!
changes.TT4/g5/r0: It's too late. No pulse. His pupils are dilated. Man: Young master!!
changes.TT4/g5/r1: Voice: He must not die. Me: Who's there?! Voice: God has chosen him for a sacred purpose. Please… use your gift.
changes.TT4/g5/r5: He stares with his mouth hanging open.
changes.TT4/g5/r7: What were the independent cities of ancient Greece called?
changes.TT4/g5/r10: Which city was Athens' great rival?
changes.TT4/g5/r11: Who was the greatest hero of Greek mythology?
changes.TT4/g5/r12: What was Athena's sacred temple called?
changes.TT4/g5/r13: The three major Greek crops were olives, grapes, and…?
changes.TT4/g5/r14: Fisher: Correct. All five! Well done.
changes.TT4/g5/r15: Fisher: Tears shed in pity are the quickest to dry… An old Greek proverb.
